title: Renewal & Expansion Check-in - Skyline Telecom
summary: Quarterly renewal check focused on capacity upgrade for 2 extra regions (EU + APAC), contract extension term options, and security posture. Customer wants predictable throughput for peak events and better regional redundancy; discussed Dedicated vs Hosted routing, autoscaling, and price tiers. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send revised pricing, run a targeted throughput benchmark, and share SOC2 + VPC deployment docs.
next_steps: Maya to send updated pricing for Reserved Dedicated capacity + add-on regions by 2027-11-05
Diego to schedule capacity benchmark run in EU region w/ Skyline test set (target week of 2027-11-08)
Maya to include contract amendment options (12 vs 24 month) and optional burst credits
Redwood to share SOC 2 and VPC deployment checklist with Leah by 2027-11-03
action_items: Maya Chen - Send updated pricing & expansion proposal - 2027-11-05
Diego Ramos - Run EU throughput benchmark & share results - 2027-11-12
Leah Kim - Provide list of compliance questions for SOC2/KMS - 2027-11-04
Tom Becker - Provision test accounts and routing rules for benchmark - 2027-11-08
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, we got Aisha, Tom, Leah from Skyline?
[00:07] Aisha Rahman: Yep that's correct, hey Maya, Diego, thanks for doing this. We've got about 45 minutes, I think?
[00:12] Diego Ramos: Yeah we scheduled 54 but should be fine, we can keep to the agenda.
[00:18] Tom Becker: Quick note — we've got the core renewal in six weeks so want to align on capacity soon.
[00:23] Maya Chen: Totally. Agenda: renewal term options, expansion to EU and APAC regions, capacity sizing for peak events, and security/compliance items. Diego will cover the technical sizing.
[00:33] Diego Ramos: Cool. Today we looked at your usage patterns, Aisha, and the big events are Q1 marketing blasts where you go from 200 req/s to 1,400 req/s across chat and embeddings. Right now you're on hosted with auto-scaling but burst costs spike.
[00:45] Aisha Rahman: Right, the spike pricing last quarter was a surprise. We want predictable unit cost and lower tail latency in EU.
[00:52] Leah Kim: And from security, we need VPC routing for the private deployment plus KMS integration. Also SOC2 artifacts for procurement.
[00:58] Maya Chen: Understood. Two levers: Dedicated reserved capacity to smooth unit cost and reduce tail latency, and optionally VPC/private for strict isolation. Diego, can you quickly explain how Dedicated would handle the bursts?
[01:10] Diego Ramos: Sure. With Dedicated you reserve a GPU pool that gives predictable throughput; we can configure burst capacity for 20-30% extra on top of committed. Also smart routing lets us route EU traffic to EU Dedicated nodes, reducing cross-region hops. There's also autoscale policies, but they're bounded by the reserved pool unless you enable burst credits.
[01:30] Tom Becker: Is the burst credit automatically available or an add-on?
[01:34] Maya Chen: It's an add-on typically, or part of higher-tier SLAs. We'll include options in pricing.
[01:38] Aisha Rahman: For the EU, do you have capacity in Frankfurt? We need GDPR-aligned data residency.
[01:44] Diego Ramos: Yes Frankfurt and Amsterdam options; we can pin to EU-only model variants. Note: pinned model variants may have slightly older quantization; we saw 3-5% latency variation.
[01:55] Leah Kim: That's OK as long as it's consistent. Also need audit logs and KMS key rotation support.
[02:01] Maya Chen: We support KMS and HSM integrations; Diego will share the VPC deployment checklist. Leah, anything specific on SOC2 docs you need?
[02:09] Leah Kim: SOC2 Type II report and SIEM integration details, plus a network diagram for the VPC peering.
[02:16] Maya Chen: We'll send those. Back to capacity — Diego, show the rough numbers for required GPUs.
[02:22] Diego Ramos: Based on current token/time distributions and peak concurrency of 1,400 req/s, we recommend initial Dedicated pool sized for sustained 900 req/s with burst credits to 1,600 for peak 2 hour windows. That maps to approx 12 A100-style vGPUs in our sizing sim — we'll provide exact cost with the proposal.
[02:41] Tom Becker: 12 seems reasonable; can you run an actual benchmark in EU with our prompts? We want to measure real tokens and tail latencies.
[02:48] Diego Ramos: Yes, we can run a targeted throughput benchmark. We'll need test keys and a copied prompt set — that was in the doc you shared, right Aisha?
[02:56] Aisha Rahman: Yes, uploaded to the shared folder. Tom will provision test accounts.
[03:00] Tom Becker: I'll get that done by next Tuesday.
[03:04] Maya Chen: Great. On contract terms, we usually offer 12 or 24 month reserved contracts. 24 month gives ~15% discount and includes one free region addition after year one. 12 month is more flexible.
[03:16] Aisha Rahman: We're leaning 24 months if the price is right and we get the EU+APAC regions included or cheap add-ons.
[03:23] Maya Chen: We'll price both and include an add-on table for regions. Also include burst credits pricing and SLA tiers.
[03:30] Leah Kim: For procurement we also need the data processing addendum and standard liability limits — any special clauses for telecom customers?
[03:39] Maya Chen: Nothing special beyond the standard DPA, but we can add a telecom addendum if needed. I'll loop Legal if you want custom language.
[03:46] Aisha Rahman: Might be helpful. Also curious about model fallbacks — if EU Dedicated capacity is saturated, can we route to a compatible hosted model in another region?
[03:56] Diego Ramos: Yes, smart routing supports fallback to compatible model variants in another region; you can define policy based on latency vs cost. There is a 50-150ms extra hop usual penalty depending on region.
[04:06] Tom Becker: That seems fine as a temporary measure.
[04:09] Maya Chen: On observability, our Console gives per-route token cost and tail latency histograms; we can set alerts for regression on a specific prompt set.
[04:18] Aisha Rahman: Good, we'll want those alerts.
[04:21] Maya Chen: Quick pause — Leah, Diego will share the security checklist after this call. Any other compliance asks?
[04:27] Leah Kim: Just encryption at transit/rest, CMK options, and a list of sub-processors.
[04:33] Diego Ramos: We'll include that in the doc bundle.
[04:36] Aisha Rahman: About pricing — can you provide a blended per-token estimate for our current mix (chat 60%, embeddings 30%, rerank 10)? We need that for our finance review.
[04:46] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll provide blended estimates for Hosted vs Dedicated (committed) and show savings with reserved capacity.
[04:52] Tom Becker: Also include a sensitivity table showing cost at 0.5x, 1x, 2x load.
[04:58] Diego Ramos: Yep.
[05:00] Maya Chen: Next steps recap: I'll send updated pricing and contract amendment options, Diego will run the EU benchmark and share results, Leah to send the compliance question list, Tom to provision test accounts. Anything else?
[05:12] Aisha Rahman: Could you also include a draft statement of work for the migration tasks — routing, DNS, certs — so our infra team can review?
[05:20] Maya Chen: Absolutely, we'll add a SOW draft.
[05:23] Ravi Patel: One small ask — can we add a staging window for switching traffic? We'd like a canary policy.
[05:29] Diego Ramos: We support canary rollouts and traffic splitting; we'll include recommended rollback thresholds.
[05:35] Tom Becker: Solid. Timeline — can we aim to finalize pricing and run benchmark in the next two weeks? Our procurement cycle is ~3 weeks after pricing.
[05:44] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll target pricing by 2027-11-05 and benchmark the week of 2027-11-08. Is that OK for everyone?
[05:52] Aisha Rahman: Works for us.
[05:55] Leah Kim: Works.
[05:56] Maya Chen: Great. I'll follow up with the doc bundle and pricing. Thanks everyone.
[05:59] Aisha Rahman: Thanks Maya and Diego. Bye.
